previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, chronic pancreatitis, atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for epigastric abdominal pain, fever, and lethargy. He presented with tachycardia, fever to 103.8°F, and abdominal distension. Initial concerns included possible sepsis, small bowel obstruction, and pneumonia. CT showed dilated small bowel loops concerning for partial obstruction, but the patient continued passing gas and stool, suggesting ileus rather than mechanical blockage. Chest imaging revealed pulmonary edema likely from heart failure. Broad-spectrum antibiotics were started but discontinued after no infection source was found and blood cultures remained negative. His symptoms improved with hemodialysis, which removed excess fluid, and a bowel regimen. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate was controlled with diltiazem. He received one unit of blood for anemia and was managed for hypercalcemia related to secondary hyperparathyroidism. By discharge, he was afebrile, ambulatory with assistance, and had resumed normal bowel function. He was discharged home with instructions on fluid restriction, medication adherence, and follow-up for calcium and hemoglobin monitoring.
